The '''2022–23 season''' was [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea Football Club]]'s [[List of Chelsea F.C. seasons|117th year in existence]] and 34th consecutive season in the top flight of [[Football in England|English football]]. In addition to the [[2022–23 Premier League|domestic league]], Chelsea participated in this season's editions of the [[2022–23 FA Cup|FA Cup]], [[2022–23 EFL Cup|EFL Cup]] and [[2022–23 UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League]].<ref>{{cite web|title=History|url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/about-chelsea/history|publisher=Chelsea F.C.|date=1 July 2020}}</ref>

The season covers the period from 1 July 2022 to 30 June 2023. This was the first full season under new owner and chairman [[Todd Boehly]] after he officially acquired the club on 30 May 2022, making it the first season since [[2002–03 Chelsea F.C. season|2002–03]] without [[Roman Abramovich]]. It was also the first time in Chelsea's history that they were under four different managers in a single season. As Chelsea finished in 12th place, this was the first season since [[1995–96 Chelsea F.C. season|1995–96]] that the team failed to finish in the top half of the league table and the club's lowest league finish since ending the [[1993–94 Chelsea F.C. season|1993–94]] season in 14th place.

==Season summary==
On 23 May, it was announced that long-serving goalkeeping coach Christophe Lollichon would leave the club after having joined from Rennes in 2007 to help with the training of former goalkeeper [[Petr Čech]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Fond farewell to long-serving goalkeeper coach Lollichon |url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/news/2022/05/23/fond-farewell-to-long-serving-goalkeeper-coach-lollichon |access-date=24 May 2022 |publisher=Chelsea F.C.}}</ref>

On 28 May, Chelsea released a statement via the club website stating that "Chelsea Football Club can confirm that a final and definitive agreement was entered into last night to sell the Club to the Todd Boehly/Clearlake Capital consortium. It was expected that the transaction would be completed on Monday."<ref>{{cite news |title=Chelsea Release club statement on sale of Club. |url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/news/2022/05/28/club-statement |publisher=Chelsea F.C.}}</ref> The consortium led by [[Todd Boehly]], chairman and CEO of [[Eldridge Industries]], and Clearlake Capital, announced completion of the ownership transfer of Chelsea on 30 May 2022. The consortium also includes [[Hansjörg Wyss]], founder of the Wyss Foundation, and [[Mark Walter]], co-founder and CEO of [[Guggenheim Partners]]. Walter and Boehly are partial owners of the [[Los Angeles Dodgers]], the [[Los Angeles Lakers]], and the [[Los Angeles Sparks]]. The transaction has received all necessary approvals from The Government of the United Kingdom, The Premier League, and other authorities.<ref>{{cite news |title=Consortium led by Todd Boehly and Clearlake Capital completes acquisition of Chelsea Football Club |url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/news/2022/05/30/consortium-led-by-todd-boehly-and-clearlake-capital-completes-ac |access-date=30 May 2022 |publisher=Chelsea F.C.}}</ref>

It was announced on 20 June that long-serving Chairman [[Bruce Buck]] would step-down after 19 years in the role effective on 30 June.<ref>{{cite news |title=Bruce Buck to step down as Chairman of Chelsea Football Club |url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/news/2022/06/20/bruce-buck-to-step-down-as-chairman-of-chelsea-football-club |publisher=Chelsea F.C. |date=20 June 2022}}</ref> A further statement was released on 22 June announcing a new-look Board of Directors including Boehly, Eghbali, Feliciano, Walter, Wyss as well as [[Jonathan Goldstein (businessman)|Jonathan Goldstein]], [[Barbara Charone]], [[Daniel Finkelstein]] and James Pade. It was also revealed that long serving [[Marina Granovskaia]] left the club, with Boehly acting as interim Sporting Director as well as chairman.<ref>{{cite news |title=Chelsea Football Club announces new Board of Directors and leadership changes |url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/news/2022/06/22/chelsea-football-club-announces-new-board-of-directors |publisher=Chelsea F.C. |date=22 June 2022}}</ref> The club then announced on 27 June that Petr Čech would leave his role as technical and performance advisor at the end of the month.<ref>{{cite news |title=Petr Cech to leave Technical and Performance Advisor role |url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/news/2022/06/27/petr-cech-to-leave-technical-and-performance-advisor-role |date=27 June 2022 |access-date=27 June 2022 |publisher=Chelsea F.C.}}</ref>

On 13 July, Chelsea announced their first signing of the season, with English international winger [[Raheem Sterling]] joining the club for a reported fee of £47.5 million.<ref name=Sterling>{{cite news |title=Raheem Sterling: Chelsea sign forward from Man City for £47.5m |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11668/12647321/raheem-sterling-chelsea-sign-forward-from-manchester-city-for-47-5m |access-date=13 July 2022 |publisher=Sky Sports}}</ref> Three days later, they completed the signing of [[Kalidou Koulibaly]] for a reported fee of £33 million.<ref name=Koulibaly>{{cite news |title=Kalidou Koulibaly: Chelsea complete deal for Napoli centre back |url=https://www.skysports.com/transfer/news/12691/12651214/kalidou-koulibaly-chelsea-complete-deal-for-napoli-centre-back |access-date=16 July 2022 |publisher=Sky Sports}}</ref>

In the first match of the new [[2022–23 Premier League|Premier League season]], Chelsea defeated [[Everton F.C.|Everton]] 1–0 at [[Goodison Park]], with [[Jorginho (footballer, born December 1991)|Jorginho]] scoring a penalty.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/62358042|title=Everton 0–1 Chelsea: Jorginho's penalty sets Chelsea on road to victory at Goodison Park|date=6 August 2022|access-date=15 August 2022|website=BBC Sport}}</ref> The second game of the season saw Chelsea face their [[Chelsea F.C.-Tottenham Hotspur F.C. rivalry|North London rivals]] [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]] at [[Stamford Bridge (stadium)|Stamford Bridge]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/match/_/gameId/638213/tottenham-hotspur-chelsea|title=Chelsea 2-2 Spurs|date=14 August 2022|access-date=12 November 2025|website=BBC Sport}}</ref> After a relatively quiet first half, Chelsea went into the break 1–0 up courtesy of defender Kalidou Koulibaly's first goal for the club – a volley from a [[Marc Cucurella]] corner. Tottenham Hotspur midfielder [[Pierre-Emile Højbjerg]] equalised in the 68th minute, with Chelsea players and manager, [[Thomas Tuchel]], unhappy that [[Kai Havertz]] had been fouled in the build-up to the goal, as well as Tottenham Hotspur forward [[Richarlison]] being in an offside position and obstructing Chelsea goalkeeper [[Édouard Mendy]]'s view of Højbjerg's shot. In the aftermath of the goal, Tuchel squared up to Tottenham Hotspur manager, and former Chelsea boss, [[Antonio Conte]], after Conte's exuberant celebrations. Both managers were shown yellow cards.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/62543119|title=Chelsea 2-2 Tottenham: Thomas Tuchel says 'match sucked me in' as he and Antonio Conte saw red|date=14 August 2022|access-date=14 August 2022|website=BBC Sport}}</ref> Chelsea regained the lead through right-back [[Reece James (footballer, born 1999)|Reece James]]' composed finish in the 77th minute. Tottenham Hotspur equalised again in the 96th minute, after [[Harry Kane]] had headed in from a corner. Once again, Tuchel and the Chelsea players were unhappy that Tottenham Hotspur defender [[Cristian Romero (footballer, born 1998)|Cristian Romero]] had pulled on Marc Cucurella's hair at the previous corner – an incident which had been reviewed by [[Video assistant referee|VAR]] referee [[Mike Dean (referee)|Mike Dean]].<ref name=espn>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.co.uk/football/english-premier-league/story/4721834/anthony-taylor-shouldnt-officiate-chelsea-matches-thomas-tuchel|title=Anthony Taylor shouldn't officiate Chelsea matches - Thomas Tuchel|first=James|last=Olley|date=14 August 2022|access-date=14 August 2022|website=ESPN}}</ref> Both the referee and VAR admitted a mistake was made, during the hair pulling incident. Following the full-time whistle, there was another heated confrontation between Tuchel and Conte, with referee [[Anthony Taylor (referee)|Anthony Taylor]] showing both straight red cards. In his post-match press conference, Tuchel stated that he was frustrated with the refereeing decisions against his team, and when asked about the supporters' view that Taylor has a history of making decisions against Chelsea, he replied: "I don't think just some of the fans think that. I can assure you the whole dressing room of us, every single person, thinks that".<ref name=espn/> He went on to say that "of course" his players were worried when they had learned of Taylor's appointment to this game, and replied "maybe it would be better" when asked if Taylor should not referee Chelsea games in future.<ref name=espn/> In the third league match, Chelsea travelled to [[Elland Road]] to face [[Chelsea F.C.-Leeds United F.C. rivalry|rivals]] [[Leeds United F.C.|Leeds United]] and suffered a heavy 3–0 defeat, the first of the season, leaving them five points behind league leaders [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/62537747|title=Leeds 3-0 Chelsea: Hosts dominate at Elland Road to continue unbeaten start|date=21 August 2022|access-date=21 August 2022|website=BBC Sport}}</ref>

During the first week of September long time serving head of international scouting Scott McLachlan left the club. He had been on gardening leave for three months after being in his post for the last eleven years – during which he oversaw both the men's and youth recruitment during a significant portion of the Roman Abramovich era.<ref>{{cite news |last=Kinsella |first=Nizaar |date=3 September 2022 |title=Behind the scenes Chelsea overhaul continues with another departure |url=https://www.standard.co.uk/sport/football/scott-mclachlan-chelsea-fc-latest-news-2022-b1022962.html |access-date=4 September 2022 |publisher=Evening Standard}}</ref> 

On 6 September, Chelsea started their [[2022–23 UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League]] campaign away to [[GNK Dinamo Zagreb|Dinamo Zagreb]], losing 1–0.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/62800323|title=Dinamo Zagreb 1-0 Chelsea: Mislav Orsic scores winner in Group E opener|date=6 September 2022|access-date=6 September 2022|website=BBC Sport}}</ref> Shortly after the loss, Tuchel was sacked by the club.<ref>{{cite news |title=Chelsea Football Club part company with Thomas Tuchel |url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/news/article/chelsea-football-club-part-company-with-thomas-tuchel |access-date=8 September 2022 |publisher=Chelsea F.C.}}</ref> 

On 8 September, Chelsea announced Graham Potter as their new head coach.<ref>{{cite news |title=Welcome to Chelsea, Graham Potter! |url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/news/article/welcome-to-chelsea-graham-potter |access-date=8 September 2022 |publisher=Chelsea F.C.}}</ref> 
Potter's debut match for Chelsea saw the Blues’ draw against [[FC Red Bull Salzburg|Red Bull Salzburg]] 1–1 in a home Champions League match, with a Raheem Sterling goal.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/62895693|title=Chelsea 1-1 FC Red Bull Salzburg: Hosts held to draw on Potter's first outing as manager|date=14 September 2022|access-date=14 September 2022|website=BBC Sport}}</ref> In Potter's second match, Chelsea defeated [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]] 2–1 away from home. In his third match in charge, Chelsea trounced [[A.C. Milan|Milan]] 3–0 at Stamford Bridge, improving their position in the Champions League. They also won the reverse fixture away from home 2–0 top go top of their group. In between the two UCL games, Chelsea easily dispatched of [[Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C.|Wolverhampton]], 3–0. Chelsea's good form continued, as they defeated [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]] 2–0 on the road, with a [[Mason Mount]] brace. Overall, Potter won five and drew one of his first six matches in charge.

However, in the next 20 league matches, Chelsea only managed 4 wins and eight draws, while sustaining eight losses. As a result, team dropped to 11th and Graham Potter was sacked on 2 April 2023 following a 0–2 home defeat to Aston Villa. Chelsea were also out of both the Carabao Cup and FA Cup after losing to [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] in the third round of both competitions although they unexpectedly knocked out [[Borussia Dortmund]] in the Champions League round of 16 (0–1 away, 2–0 home). He was replaced by caretaker [[Bruno (footballer, born 1980)|Bruno Saltor]] until 6 April,<ref name="Club Statement"/> when an interim, [[Frank Lampard]], was hired until the end of the season.<ref name="Club statement - Frank Lampard"/> Lampard had already led Chelsea in the [[2019–20 Chelsea F.C. season|2019–20]] and the first half of [[2020–21 Chelsea F.C. season|2020–21]] seasons. In Lampard's first match on 8 April 2023, Chelsea lost 0–1 in an away game against [[Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C.|Wolves]].<ref>[https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11661/12850605/wolves-1-0-chelsea-frank-lampard-starts-caretaker-role-with-defeat-after-stunning-matheus-nunes-volley Report and free match highlights as Frank Lampard's first game as Chelsea caretaker manager ends in a 1-0 defeat at Molineux; Matheus Nunes scores stunning first-half volley to lift Wolves four points above the relegation zone; Chelsea are 11th and 17 points off the top four]</ref>

Chelsea ended the season in 12th place after only managing 1 win and 2 draws, while sustaining 6 losses, in their nine league games under Lampard ending with a home draw to [[Newcastle United]], capping off a turbulent first season under new ownership. As they had also been knocked out of the Champions League after losing 4–0 on aggregate to Real Madrid in the quarter-finals, they did not participate in European football the following season for the first time since [[2016–17 Chelsea F.C. season|2016–17]], the most recent time they won the Premier League.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Sodeeq |first=Yemi |date=2023-05-28 |title=Chelsea to miss out from European competitions first time since 2016/17 season |url=https://theinformant247.com/chelsea-to-miss-out-from-european-competitions-first-time-since-2016-17-season/ |location=Kwara, Nigeria|access-date=2023-08-18 |newspaper=[[The Informant247]]|language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Sritharan |first=Joel |date=2023-04-18 |title=Chelsea out of Europe: Last time Blues missed out and failed to qualify for UEFA cup competitions |url=https://www.sportingnews.com/us/soccer/news/chelsea-in-europe-history-uefa-champions-league-qualify/ahvsfygii4v3l12km0apcjh5 |access-date=2023-08-18 |website=[[Sporting News]] |language=en-us}}</ref>

==Pre-season and friendlies==
Chelsea announced they would travel to the [[United States]] to take part in the [[Florida Cup (soccer)|FC Series]] with a friendly against [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Chelsea to play Arsenal in Orlando pre-season fixture |url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/news/2022/04/19/chelsea-to-play-arsenal-in-orlando-pre-season-fixture |access-date=21 April 2022 |publisher=Chelsea F.C. |date=19 April 2022}}</ref> A month later the club announced two further fixtures as part of the FC Series, against [[Club América|América]] and [[Charlotte FC]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Chelsea to play in Las Vegas and Charlotte as part of USA pre-season tour |url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/news/2022/05/18/chelsea-to-play-in-las-vegas-and-charlotte-as-part-of-usa-pre-se |access-date=18 May 2022 |publisher=Chelsea F.C. |date=18 May 2022}}</ref> On 6 July, Chelsea confirmed they would play [[Udinese Calcio|Udinese]] in [[Italy]] after the American tour.<ref>{{cite news |title=Chelsea to play pre-season match in Italy |url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/news/article/chelsea-to-play-pre-season-match-in-italy |date=6 July 2022 |access-date=7 July 2022 |publisher=Chelsea F.C. }}</ref>

During the mid-season winter break, The club announced a friendly with [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]] in [[Abu Dhabi]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Chelsea to play in Abu Dhabi again! |url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/news/article/chelsea-to-play-in-abu-dhabi-again |access-date=28 November 2022 |publisher=Chelsea F.C. |date=24 November 2022}}</ref>

====Knockout phase====
{{main|2022–23 UEFA Champions League knockout phase}}

=====Round of 16=====
The round of 16 draw was held on 7 November 2022.

Chelsea were drawn against German side [[Borussia Dortmund]] in the round of 16, with the first leg away from home as they progressed as group winners.<ref>{{cite news |title=German opponents for Chelsea in Champions League last-16 |url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/news/article/german-opponents-for-chelsea-in-champions-league-last-16 |access-date=7 November 2022 |publisher=Chelsea F.C. |date=7 November 2022}}</ref>

=====Quarter-finals=====
The quarter-finals draw was held on 17 March 2023.

Chelsea were drawn against Spanish side and defending champions [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]], with the first leg away from home.<ref>{{cite news |title=Dates announced for Chelsea's Champions League quarter-final |url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/news/article/chelsea-discover-champions-league-quarter-final-opponents |access-date=17 March 2023 |publisher=Chelsea F.C. |date=17 March 2023}}</ref>
